title: Stack SMS and Slack decorators on an email notifier

blocks.text: The page's notifiers: an `EmailNotifier` is the component, and SMS and Slack are decorators that implement the same `Notifier` interface, delegate to the notifier they wrap and then add their own part. The page's first pitfall is a decorator that forgets to delegate, so **every method delegates to the wrapped notifier**, `getDescription()` as much as `send()`.

items: `NotifierDecorator`, an abstract base that keeps the wrapped notifier and passes both methods on. **A `null` wrappee is refused in the constructor** with `NullPointerException`.
`SmsDecorator(wrappee, phone)`: `send` returns the wrapped result followed by `" | SMS to <phone>: <message>"`; the description adds `" + SMS(<phone>)"`.

blocks.text: Decorators stack in any combination, and **the same decorator applied twice adds its part twice**.

rows: `Email to a@example.org: alert | SMS to +1: alert`
`... | SMS to +1: alert | SMS to +2: alert`

cases.says: Slack(Sms(Email)).send("alert") returns the email text, then the SMS part, then the Slack part, joined by " | ".
getDescription also goes through every layer: Slack(Sms(Email)) describes itself as "Email(a@example.org) + SMS(+1) + Slack(#ops)".
Sms(Sms(Email, "+1"), "+2") sends to both numbers, one part per layer.
new SmsDecorator(null, "+1") and new SlackDecorator(null, "ops") throw NullPointerException immediately.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

concepts: An abstract base decorator holds the wrapped component and passes every method on, so concrete decorators override only what they change.
A decorator's constructor refuses a null wrapped component.
A decorator implements the same interface as the component it wraps, delegates every operation to it and adds its own behaviour before or after.
Decorators stack in any combination at run time, and applying the same decorator twice has a cumulative effect.
